clue.text: Chimp perhaps takes fruit to consume inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for consuming is placed within the fruit word

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A chimpanzee grabs some fruit to eat indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to consume inside' puts EAT within GRAPE; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is one example of the large primates also called anthropoids, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: One who tries out rodent eaten in Peru

definitions.meaning: someone used for testing a new idea or product on, a test subject
the cavy, a small South American rodent that is a traditional dish in Peru

explanation.surface: A food critic samples a local delicacy on a trip to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the first sense is one who is tried out on, but the setter treats a test subject as the one doing the trying.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavy is both a household pet and a stock phrase for any experimental subject.

clue.text: When light's dropped and left in broken pieces

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the rearranged letters
broken pieces are jumbled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lamp has fallen and lies smashed to bits on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns PIECES into ECIPSE, and 'in' sets L within it.
explanation.definitionFit: During a solar or lunar eclipse the light falls away as one body blocks another.

clue.text: Simple garment less than thirty shillings inside

indicators.note: inside puts the shillings abbreviation within the shortened number
less than here means the word thirty falls short by its final letter

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for shillings in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A plain garment priced at under thirty shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' removes Y from THIRTY to leave THIRT, and 'inside' puts S in it. A shilling was a British coin before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved collarless top is about the plainest everyday garment there is.

clue.text: Large perennial, but it doesn't sound ornamental

definitions.text: Large perennial, but it doesn't sound ornamental

parts.words: Large perennial, but it doesn't sound ornamental
parts.note: a big long-lived tree whose first word, said aloud, is the same as a word meaning unadorned, not ornamental

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a big hardy plant lacks showy flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of this tree sounds like 'plain', the opposite of ornamental.
explanation.definitionFit: This broad-leaved tree, common in London streets, is a large long-lived woody perennial.

clue.text: Area covered by short superficial beauty treatment

indicators.note: covered by puts the area letter inside the shortened adjective
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: facile means superficial, shallow

explanation.surface: A quick, shallow beauty treatment that only touches the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts FACILE to FACIL, and 'covered by' puts A inside it, after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatment of cleansing and massage for the face is a staple beauty-salon service.

clue.text: Opponent father mentioned in social blunder

indicators.note: mentioned signals that the words are heard spoken, not written

parts.note: a foe is an opponent and pa is father, together said like the French phrase

explanation.surface: Someone's rival's dad comes up in conversation and causes an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: FOE PA spoken matches the French phrase, whose X and S are silent.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing literally means a false step, a tactless social error.

clue.text: About the raising of fat bishop's seat

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: lard is pork fat

explanation.surface: A corpulent bishop's chair is hoisted off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising of' turns LARD up into DRAL, after CA and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal church of a diocese houses the bishop's throne, or cathedra, from which it is named.

clue.text: Hostess, perhaps narrowly, avoided accident while flying

definitions.meaning: a flight attendant could jokingly be called a young lady of the skies
a near collision between aircraft in flight

explanation.surface: A stewardess has a close shave on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The aviation term for a near collision of aircraft also reads as a young woman working on board.

clue.text: Ailing steel plant losing millions

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is taken away from the factory word

parts.note: a steel mill is a steel plant
M is the abbreviation for million(s); the answer's letters also sitting inside this word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A struggling steelworks is haemorrhaging millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes M from MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailing and its synonym both mean unwell, in poor health.

clue.text: Recruiting agent kept watch, bringing in leader for executives

indicators.note: bringing in tells us the word for kept takes a letter inside it

parts.note: had is a past tense of have, kept or held

indicators.note: leader for picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover over the face

explanation.surface: A recruiter, after keeping an eye out, brings in a new boss for the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' puts E (first of executives) inside HAD, giving HEAD. A hunter is a pocket watch with a metal lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruitment consultant who poaches senior staff for other firms gets this nickname.

clue.text: Vote on English ale, one selling overseas

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the vote letter follows the English letter

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: At the pub, someone voting on English beer turns out to sell abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets X after E; then comes PORTER, a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sends goods to foreign markets for sale is so described.

clue.text: Cry when wheeling? It's a lapwing

definitions.meaning: the call a plover gives as it wheels in flight
a crested plover of fields and moors

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher identifies a circling bird by its call.
explanation.walkthrough: The lapwing is named for its call, so one word covers both the bird and its cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing's other name imitates its plaintive two-note call.

clue.text: Mole that is infiltrating public relations

indicators.note: infiltrating puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A spy has been planted in the PR department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the spy of the surface, but it is a harbour breakwater; 'infiltrating' puts IE inside PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone breakwater or jetty, a structure jutting out into the sea.

clue.text: Scent upsetting to wearers

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A perfume that offends the people who wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges the nine letters of TO WEARERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Water distilled with petals is a fragrance used in perfumery and cookery.

clue.text: What transvestite does to thwart coercion, leaving university

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart them

indicators.note: leaving means the university letter goes out of the word for coercion

parts.note: duress is coercion, pressure by threats

explanation.surface: A transvestite's dressing habit is described as a way to resist pressure, after dropping out of college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops U from DURESS to leave DRESS, after CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing clothes usually worn by the opposite sex is the defining habit described.

clue.text: Overweight? Putting in roadwork, good and prolonged

indicators.note: putting in places the other pieces inside the word for overweight

parts.note: stout means fat, overweight
roadwork is a boxer's training by running on roads

explanation.surface: Someone fat takes up roadwork, which is good, and keeps at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting in' sets RUN and G inside STOUT. Roadwork is a boxer's running training, not digging up the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread thin over a long stretch of time or space is prolonged.

clue.text: Captured odd military instrument

parts.note: snared means trapped, captured
rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A strange musical instrument has been taken from the army.
explanation.definitionFit: This side drum with wires across its lower head is standard in military bands.

clue.text: Fruit Adam and Eve alone would not have appreciated?

definitions.text: Adam and Eve alone would not have appreciated?
definitions.meaning: an unwanted third person tagging along with a couple who want privacy

explanation.surface: The first couple, alone in Eden, disliked a certain fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: To play this fruit is a British idiom for being the unwanted third person with a courting couple; the Eden apple is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The berry and the idiom for a third wheel share one word.

clue.text: Old wrought iron company resident on Wimbledon Common

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An old ironworks company is based on a London common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought' rearranges IRON into RINO. The Wombles, from a British children's series, live on Wimbledon Common; this is one of them, named after a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This furry creature of children's books and television lives with the other Wombles on Wimbledon Common.

clue.text: In plain, gunners finally unleashing bombardment

indicators.note: In tells us the pieces go inside the word for plain

parts.note: bare means plain, unadorned
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Out on the plain the artillery at last open fire.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and G, the last letter of 'unleashing', go inside BARE. 'finally' looks like it belongs to gunners but takes the end of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy continuous burst of artillery fire is a bombardment.

clue.text: I'm in the French capital

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Paris, but 'the French' is LA, and IM goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Peru.

clue.text: What opens its petals over morning or early afternoon

definitions.text: What opens its petals over morning or early afternoon

indicators.note: what opens each word is its first letter, taken from the seven words that follow

explanation.surface: A description of a flower that unfolds in the morning or soon after noon.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the last seven words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus includes morning glory, whose flowers open early in the day.

clue.text: Observer's editor only partly shows experience

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective: one who shows experience is skilled

indicators.note: only partly means just a run of letters inside the words is used

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor shows only some of what they know.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Observer's editor'. The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well practised or knowledgeable in a subject is demonstrating experience in it.

clue.text: One seeing six sheep by river

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Someone watches six sheep beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks at or watches something, such as television, is an onlooker.

clue.text: English pen love letters sent out in this?

definitions.text: English pen love letters sent out in this?

indicators.note: sent out means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone posts love letters written with an English pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges PEN LOVE into NVELOPE, after E; the whole clue describes what letters are posted in.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper wrapper is what letters are posted in.

clue.text: Double firsts from Oxford University struggling with Greats? Grossly undignified

indicators.note: struggling with means the letters are wrestled together into a new order
double means the pair of letters is taken twice
firsts from picks the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Oxford student with double firsts struggles through the Greats course.
explanation.walkthrough: OU twice plus GREATS are rearranged together. Greats is the Oxford degree in classics; a 'double first' is top marks in two exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking or beyond all decency describes behaviour that is grossly undignified.

clue.text: One in eight or three in 27

indicators.note: three in means a run of three letters inside the answer to clue 27

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is the word for rough-speaking

explanation.surface: A riddle about counting members of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight; the answer also appears as the middle three letters of 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight has eight rowers, each pulling one blade.

clue.text: Hackney possibly sounded rough-speaking

indicators.note: sounded tells us the word is heard said aloud

parts.note: a hackney is a breed of carriage horse

explanation.surface: Someone from Hackney in London has a rasping voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of London, but here it is a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, croaky voice describes someone speaking huskily.

clue.text: Boss that's very distant with head of ministry breeding establishment

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob
far means very distant

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An aloof boss teams up with the head of a ministry at a breeding centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is a raised knob, like a stud, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where horses are kept for breeding is this kind of farm.
